questions.scenario: A friend twists their ankle badly during a tense game of gully cricket or football. What is your reaction?

options.text: You immediately run over, tell them not to move it, grab some ice, and spray Volini or Moov like a pro.
You ask exactly how they twisted it and at what angle, trying to mentally figure out which specific ligament took the impact.
You distract them with a joke to stop them from crying, while gently helping them limp to the side of the road.
You take charge, find a nearby scooty or auto to take them home, and figure out who will pay the local doctor's fee.

questions.scenario: Your Dadi or Nani complains of severe knee pain while climbing the stairs at home. What do you do?

options.text: You gently massage her calves with warm oil and physically help her climb step-by-step by holding her arm.
You watch her walking pattern (gait) closely and realize she's putting too much body weight on her left heel.
You turn her daily walking exercise into a fun, slow-motion game with you so she forgets the pain and enjoys the process.
You convince your parents to finally buy that expensive electric knee-support massager machine you saw on Amazon.

questions.scenario: Everyone in your class is complaining about neck and shoulder pain because of super heavy school bags. What's your solution?

options.text: You practically demonstrate a quick neck stretch and shoulder roll exercise you learned to relieve their tension.
You analyze the center of gravity and explain how tightening the bag straps will fix their spinal alignment.
You invent a funny 'zombie walk' game during the recess to help everyone stretch their stiff backs while laughing.
You draft a formal petition to the Principal demanding lockers in school so students don't have to carry textbooks daily.

questions.scenario: It's board exam prep time, and your friend is slouching like a prawn over their study table. What do you do?

options.text: You physically tap their back, tell them to sit straight, and give them a quick shoulder squeeze to relieve the tight muscles.
You explain how studying in that C-shaped position will compress their cervical spine and cause a slipped disc later in life.
You stick a funny neon sticky note on their laptop screen saying 'Sit straight or you'll turn into a turtle!'
You suggest they buy a proper ergonomic chair or a laptop stand from Flipkart to boost their long-term study efficiency.

questions.scenario: You and your friends join the local gym for the first time. What is your main focus?

options.text: Spotting your friends, making sure they lift weights with the correct form, and showing them how to stretch after the workout.
Researching the exact muscle groups activated during a bicep curl and analyzing the physics of the joint angles.
Making a fun, upbeat Bollywood dance-cardio routine because lifting heavy iron rods is too repetitive and boring.
Comparing the gym's monthly fees, checking if the treadmills are high-quality, and negotiating a group discount with the trainer.

questions.scenario: You go to a Bata or local shoe shop to buy sports shoes for the new school year. How do you pick them?

options.text: You put them on, jump around, and do a quick sprint in the shop aisle to test the physical grip and cushioning.
You check the sole's arch support to see if it properly corrects flat feet and prevents the ankle from rolling inward.
You pick the ones with the coolest bright neon colors and lights that make you feel like a superhero while running.
You check the durability, warranty tag, and argue with the shopkeeper to give you the 20% Diwali discount.

questions.scenario: You are watching an intense IPL or Pro Kabaddi match on TV, and a player gets brutally tackled.

options.text: You watch closely as the team physio rushes onto the field, secretly wishing you could be the one fixing the star player.
You rewind the slow-motion replay to analyze the exact moment the knee twisted and what physical force caused the injury.
You feel immense empathy for the player and hope they have a quick, painless recovery so they can smile and play again.
You wonder how much the team's medical insurance covers for such massive injuries and expensive surgeries.

questions.scenario: Your uncle (Chacha) has terrible lower back pain from sitting at his office desk all day.

options.text: You make him lie down on the yoga mat and demonstrate the 'Bhujangasana' (Cobra pose) to instantly stretch his back.
You explain that his pain is likely radiating from a pinched nerve (sciatica) and explain the anatomy of the spinal cord.
You joke around with him, saying his tummy is getting too big from sitting, and challenge him to a fun 30-second plank competition.
You recommend the best specialized physiotherapy clinic in your city and tell him to book a premium consultation right away.

questions.scenario: You are endlessly scrolling through Instagram Reels or YouTube Shorts. Which video makes you stop and watch?

options.text: A highly satisfying bone-cracking (chiropractic) video or an athlete getting a deep-tissue sports massage.
A detailed 3D animation showing how the human skeleton, nerves, and muscles work together when a person runs.
A heartwarming, emotional video of a disabled toddler taking their very first steps with the help of a walking frame.
A business breakdown video explaining how the healthcare, fitness, and wellness industry in India is booming into a billion-dollar market.

questions.scenario: It's the PT (Physical Training) period and the sports teacher is absent. What is your role?

options.text: You take charge, lead the class in a proper warm-up routine, and organize a high-energy, injury-free football match.
You sit on the sidelines and observe how different classmates run, noticing who has a bad running form or flat feet.
You invent a completely new, crazy game mixing Kho-Kho and Tag that gets everyone laughing, running, and burning energy.
You take the sports equipment key from the monitor, manage who gets the bats and balls, and make sure nothing gets stolen.

Sports_Physiotherapist.title: The On-Field Healer (Sports / Orthopedic Physiotherapist)
Sports_Physiotherapist.primary_match_text: You are a hands-on, action-oriented healer! You love sports, fitness, and physical movement. When someone gets hurt, you don't panic; you jump right in to fix them with your own hands.
Sports_Physiotherapist.day_in_the_life: Running onto the cricket pitch or football field to treat injured athletes, performing deep-tissue massages, taping sprained ankles, and helping players return to peak physical form.
Sports_Physiotherapist.alternative_match_text: Your love for fitness and physical action would also make you an excellent Sports Coach, Fitness Trainer, or Orthopedic Surgeon.
Sports_Physiotherapist.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Science (PCB is mandatory). Entrance: Crack NEET or State CETs. Degree: 4.5-year Bachelor of Physiotherapy (BPT). Next Steps: Master of Physiotherapy (MPT) specializing in Sports or Orthopedics.

Neuro_Physiotherapist.title: The Movement Scientist (Neuro-Physiotherapist / Biomechanics Analyst)
Neuro_Physiotherapist.primary_match_text: You are highly analytical and fascinated by the human machine. You love combining physics with biology. You don't just treat the pain; you act like a detective to find out exactly *why* the pain started.
Neuro_Physiotherapist.day_in_the_life: Studying a patient's walking pattern, treating complex nerve injuries (like paralysis or stroke recovery), analyzing joint angles, and retraining the brain to move the body correctly.
Neuro_Physiotherapist.alternative_match_text: Your logical brain makes you a perfect fit for fields like Biomedical Engineering, Neuroscience, or Ergonomics Design.
Neuro_Physiotherapist.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Science (PCB). Entrance: Crack NEET or University-specific exams. Degree: 4.5-year Bachelor of Physiotherapy (BPT). Next Steps: Pursue an MPT with a specialization in Neurology or Biomechanics.

Pediatric_Physiotherapist.title: The Playful Healer (Pediatric Physiotherapist)
Pediatric_Physiotherapist.primary_match_text: You have a huge heart, high empathy, and a highly creative mind. You know that healing isn't just about medicine; it's about making people smile. You love working with children and making therapy feel like playtime.
Pediatric_Physiotherapist.day_in_the_life: Using colorful toys, bouncy balls, and fun games to help children with physical disabilities (like cerebral palsy) build their strength and learn how to walk or crawl.
Pediatric_Physiotherapist.alternative_match_text: If not physiotherapy, your empathetic and playful nature would make you a wonderful Child Psychologist, Special Educator, or Pediatrician.
Pediatric_Physiotherapist.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Science (PCB). Entrance: Crack NEET or State CETs. Degree: Bachelor of Physiotherapy (BPT). Next Steps: Master of Physiotherapy (MPT) specializing in Pediatrics.

Rehab_Center_Director.title: The Clinic Boss (Rehab Center Director / Healthcare Manager)
Rehab_Center_Director.primary_match_text: You are a natural leader with a sharp business mindset. You care about health and wellness, but you prefer managing the big picture—running the clinic, handling the money, and ensuring everything operates smoothly.
Rehab_Center_Director.day_in_the_life: Managing a massive, high-tech physiotherapy clinic, buying expensive robotic rehabilitation equipment, hiring expert doctors, and handling the business, marketing, and billing operations.
Rehab_Center_Director.alternative_match_text: Your leadership and management skills would make you an excellent Hospital Administrator, Healthcare Entrepreneur, or Medical Sales Head.
Rehab_Center_Director.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Science (PCB). Degree: Bachelor of Physiotherapy (BPT) or B.Sc Healthcare. Next Steps: Gain clinical experience, then pursue an MBA in Healthcare Management or Hospital Administration.
